morning_starts.title: Barista Parlor (East Nashville)
morning_starts.note: Where East Side songwriters nurse a pour-over and pretend they're not eavesdropping on each other's lyrics.

morning_starts.title: Crema Coffee Roasters
morning_starts.note: A downtown roaster that's been fueling early studio calls since long before the tour buses found it.

morning_starts.title: Ugly Mugs Coffee and Tea
morning_starts.note: The neighborhood living room on Woodland where half the room is scribbling verses in a notebook.

morning_starts.title: Dozen Bakery
morning_starts.note: Start with the morning bun and a coffee here and you'll forgive the world its trespasses.

morning_starts.title: Five Daughters Bakery (12South)
morning_starts.note: Grab a hundred-layer donut in 12South before the sidewalk fills up with the influencer crowd.

morning_starts.title: Elegy Coffee (East Nashville)
morning_starts.note: Quiet East Side espresso for the morning after a late writers' round runs long.

beach_lake_outdoor.title: Radnor Lake State Natural Area
beach_lake_outdoor.note: The city's front porch to nature — walk the lake loop and you'll swear the herons are keeping time.

beach_lake_outdoor.title: Warner Parks (Percy & Edwin Warner)
beach_lake_outdoor.note: Miles of shaded trails where I've hummed out more than one melody between the oaks.

beach_lake_outdoor.title: Shelby Bottoms Greenway & Nature Center
beach_lake_outdoor.note: The East Side's ribbon of green along the Cumberland — flat, easy, and full of morning birdsong.

beach_lake_outdoor.title: Long Hunter State Park - Couchville Lake
beach_lake_outdoor.business: Long Hunter State Park - Couchville Lake
beach_lake_outdoor.note: A paved lake loop out at Percy Priest where the water's still and the crowds thin out.

beach_lake_outdoor.title: Harpeth River State Park - Narrows of the Harpeth
beach_lake_outdoor.business: Harpeth River State Park - Narrows of the Harpeth
beach_lake_outdoor.note: Put a canoe on the Harpeth and let the current write the day's rhythm for you.

beach_lake_outdoor.title: Nashville Paddle Company
beach_lake_outdoor.note: Stand-up paddleboard the reservoir at sunset — best cheap therapy in Middle Tennessee.

culture_history.title: National Museum of African American Music
culture_history.business: National Museum of African American Music
culture_history.note: The heart of Jefferson Street's story — where you learn every Nashville song owes its soul to this corridor.

culture_history.title: Fisk University Galleries (Carl Van Vechten & Aaron Douglas)
culture_history.business: Fisk University Galleries (Carl Van Vechten & Aaron Douglas)
culture_history.note: The Stieglitz collection on a historic Black campus — a hushed treasure most tourists never find.

culture_history.title: Country Music Hall of Fame and Museum
culture_history.business: Country Music Hall of Fame and Museum
culture_history.note: Yes it's the big one, but stand before Hank's suit and you'll feel why we all moved here.

culture_history.title: Historic RCA Studio B
culture_history.note: Elvis cut hits in this room — stand on the floor where the Nashville Sound was actually born.

culture_history.title: The Johnny Cash Museum
culture_history.note: The most complete Cash collection anywhere, curated with real love rather than gift-shop gloss.

culture_history.title: The Parthenon
culture_history.note: A full-scale Greek temple in a city park — only in the Athens of the South, darlin'.

shopping_browsing.title: Third Man Records
shopping_browsing.note: Jack White's yellow-and-black clubhouse — cut your own record in the booth if the spirit moves you.

shopping_browsing.title: Grimey's New & Preloved Music
shopping_browsing.note: The record store where working musicians actually shop — dig the used bins for a while.

shopping_browsing.title: Hatch Show Print
shopping_browsing.note: Letterpress posters carved for the Opry stars themselves — watch the presses roll and take one home.

shopping_browsing.title: Parnassus Books
shopping_browsing.note: Ann Patchett's indie shop, where the staff picks read like letters from a wiser friend.

shopping_browsing.title: Fanny's House of Music
shopping_browsing.note: An East Side instrument shop run by folks who'll swap you a song for guitar-strap advice.

shopping_browsing.title: Fatherland District (Shoppes on Fatherland)
shopping_browsing.note: A cluster of little East Nashville makers' shops — the anti-mall, and proud of it.

casual_lunch.title: Hattie B's Hot Chicken
casual_lunch.note: Start your hot chicken education here — order medium, and don't let anyone shame you.

casual_lunch.title: Prince's Hot Chicken
casual_lunch.note: The original, the source, the church of the whole tradition — respect the heat and the history.

casual_lunch.title: Arnold's Country Kitchen
casual_lunch.note: Meat-and-three done right in a cafeteria line — the roast beef is why locals stand in it.

casual_lunch.title: Butcher & Bee
casual_lunch.note: Mezze-style plates on the East Side for when you want lunch a little lighter and greener.

casual_lunch.title: Silver Sands Cafe
casual_lunch.note: A tiny soul-food gem near the capitol — get there early before the fried green tomatoes vanish.

casual_lunch.title: The Mockingbird
casual_lunch.note: A cheeky modern diner in the Gulch — comfort food with a wink and a good playlist.

happy_hour_drinks.title: Attaboy
happy_hour_drinks.note: No menu, no sign — just tell the bartender your mood and let them write you a cocktail.

happy_hour_drinks.title: The Fox Bar & Cocktail Club
happy_hour_drinks.note: An East Side hideaway where the drinks are serious but nobody's taking themselves too seriously.

happy_hour_drinks.title: Southern Grist Brewing (East Nashville Taproom)
happy_hour_drinks.note: Wildly inventive small-batch beers in the neighborhood — go for the sours you won't find anywhere else.

happy_hour_drinks.title: Bearded Iris Brewing
happy_hour_drinks.note: Hazy IPAs in Germantown that keep the local brewers honest — grab a patio seat.

happy_hour_drinks.title: Le Loup
happy_hour_drinks.note: A candlelit wine-and-cocktail nook for the golden hour before dinner runs the show.

happy_hour_drinks.title: Acme Feed & Seed
happy_hour_drinks.note: Rooftop views over Broadway with a beer in hand — the honky-tonk chaos looks better from up here.

dinner_casual.title: Lockeland Table
dinner_casual.note: The East Nashville neighborhood restaurant — community hour cocktails, wood-fired pizza, and no pretense.

dinner_casual.title: Folk
dinner_casual.note: Wood-fired everything in a light-filled East Side room — the vegetables here sing louder than the meat.

dinner_casual.title: Hearts
dinner_casual.note: An easygoing spot where the plates are shareable and the vibe stays low-key all night.

dinner_casual.title: Party Fowl
dinner_casual.note: Hot chicken meets full bar and NFL Sundays — loud, fun, and unapologetically Nashville.

dinner_casual.title: Puckett's Grocery & Restaurant
dinner_casual.note: Southern plates with a live picker in the corner — dinner and a show for the price of dinner.

dinner_casual.title: Butcher & Bee
dinner_casual.note: Come back at night for the whipped feta and a table of small plates you'll fight over.

dinner_upscale.title: Bastion
dinner_upscale.note: A 24-seat tasting room behind a bar — one of the hardest reservations in town, and worth every call.

dinner_upscale.title: The Catbird Seat
dinner_upscale.note: Front-row seats to the chefs at work — the closest thing to a writers' round in fine dining.

dinner_upscale.title: Rolf and Daughters
dinner_upscale.note: Germantown's pasta temple — the garganelli has quietly defined Nashville dining for a decade.

dinner_upscale.title: City House
dinner_upscale.note: Tandy's belly-ham pizza in a converted studio — the chef's-night crowd knows to come Sunday.

dinner_upscale.title: Henrietta Red
dinner_upscale.note: The raw bar in Germantown — order a tower of oysters and a crisp glass, and settle in.

dinner_upscale.title: Peninsula
dinner_upscale.note: Iberian-inspired plates on the East Side that reward a long, wandering, wine-soaked evening.

dinner_romantic.title: Yolan
dinner_romantic.note: Italian fine dining in Union Station's grandeur — the room alone is worth dressing up for.

dinner_romantic.title: The Henry
dinner_romantic.note: Dim, plush, and made for leaning in close over a shared plate and a second bottle.

dinner_romantic.title: Noko
dinner_romantic.note: Live-fire Asian cooking in a warm East Side glow — the open flame does half the flirting for you.

dinner_romantic.title: Lyra
dinner_romantic.note: Eastern Mediterranean plates and candlelight — spice, smoke, and a slow-burn kind of night.

dinner_romantic.title: Bastion
dinner_romantic.note: That tiny back room feels like a secret you're keeping together — book it for someone special.

dinner_romantic.title: Peninsula
dinner_romantic.note: Order the whole fish, split the natural wine, and let the East Side evening stretch out.

nightlife.title: Robert's Western World
nightlife.note: The one honky-tonk on Broadway a local will still walk into — real traditional country, cheap beer, a fried bologna sandwich.

nightlife.title: The Station Inn
nightlife.note: Bluegrass in a cinderblock room in the Gulch — the players here are the ones the stars call to sit in.

nightlife.title: Santa's Pub
nightlife.note: Karaoke in a Christmas-lit trailer run by a man in a Santa suit — pure, unfiltered Nashville, cash only.

nightlife.title: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
nightlife.note: The purple room where Opry legends slipped in for a drink — history you can still hear through the walls.

nightlife.title: Exit/In
nightlife.note: The Rock Block's scrappy survivor — everybody from Etheridge to punk kids has played this stage.

nightlife.title: Acme Feed & Seed
nightlife.note: Three floors of bands, food, and rooftop — the sane person's way to do lower Broadway at night.

family_activities.title: The Parthenon
family_activities.note: Kids gawk at the 42-foot golden Athena while you get your art fix in Centennial Park.

family_activities.title: Cheekwood Estate & Gardens
family_activities.note: Fifty-five acres of gardens and a mansion — room for the little ones to run and the grown-ups to breathe.

family_activities.title: Grand Ole Opry House
family_activities.note: Take the whole family to the show that made country music a radio institution — a backstage tour if you can.

family_activities.title: Centennial Park
family_activities.note: Duck pond, wide lawns, and the Parthenon backdrop — the city's easiest afternoon with kids in tow.

family_activities.title: General Jackson Showboat
family_activities.note: A paddlewheel cruise down the Cumberland with a musical revue — hokey in the best possible way.

family_activities.title: Adventureworks Nashville West
family_activities.note: Ziplines and treetop courses for when the kids need to burn off their pancake breakfast.

rainy_day.title: Frist Art Museum
rainy_day.note: A grand old post office turned art hall — rotating shows and a kids' studio to wait out the storm.

rainy_day.title: National Museum of African American Music
rainy_day.business: National Museum of African American Music
rainy_day.note: Hours of interactive galleries downtown — you'll leave humming and stay dry doing it.

rainy_day.title: Country Music Hall of Fame and Museum
rainy_day.business: Country Music Hall of Fame and Museum
rainy_day.note: The rainy-day standby — you could lose a whole afternoon in here and not notice the clouds.

rainy_day.title: The Belcourt Theatre
rainy_day.note: Hillsboro Village's historic cinema — indie films and repertory classics with a real projector's glow.

rainy_day.title: The Johnny Cash Museum
rainy_day.note: Small, dry, and deeply moving — the Man in Black's whole life in one downtown block.

rainy_day.title: Parnassus Books
rainy_day.note: Duck in, grab a novel and a staff recommendation, and let the rain be somebody else's problem.
